202A.10 / CHAPTER 10 OF 11

Three basic checks

What is the thesis, what looks suspicious, and who is already in?

11 chapters with worked investigations

01Price moves at the margin02Liquidity & price impact03Buy/sell pressure04Supply transfer05Early wallet flow06Demand acceleration07Attention conversion08Push, Hold or Fail09Meta saturation10Three basic checks11How to trade the demand wave

01Definition

These are generic, minimal entry checks for any token, whether you intend to snipe, trade PvP, or swing. They provide a quick initial assessment. Passing them does not automatically justify an entry.

02Why it matters

Before shaping a trade, understand where demand could come from, how large the wave could become, and who is already positioned to sell into it.

03What to check

  • Thesis / meta / upside: what is the story, which meta does it fit, and how far could incoming demand plausibly take it from the current market cap?
  • Scam red flags: check bundle concentration, a working X link consistent with the exact contract, and any suspicious new or replacement CA. Check obvious sellability and liquidity problems.
  • Who is already in: identify notable traders, KOLs, the dev, and related wallets. Check meaningful remaining holdings and whether they are buying, holding, or selling.

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

The thesis is understandable, the contract links are consistent, and participant behavior supports the expected demand. Findings are brief, sourced, and explicit about unknowns.

Dangerous

A familiar ticker, working X link, or known-wallet badge is treated as proof of safety or as an automatic reason to buy. Bundles, a changed CA, or existing sellers are ignored.

05Beginner mistake

Turning the minimal check into a long scoring exercise, or entering simply because the token passes it.

06Takeaway

Use the same three checks for every entry. Keep this first pass minimal; deepen it and decide how to trade in 202A.11.

Thesis / meta / upside -> scam red flags -> who is already in.

A generic minimum for every entry; trading depth and execution belong in 202A.11.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    A new token fits an active story. State the source of possible fresh attention and a plausible upside case from its current valuation.

  2. 02

    Compare the exact CA with project and X links, inspect bundles, and record who still holds meaningful supply. An unresolved replacement CA is Unknown, not cleared.

  3. 03

    Summarize thesis, red flags, and participants in three short findings. Only then consider whether the expected demand supports a snipe, PvP trade, or swing.

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

An illustrative token has a clear meme thesis and a modest valuation, but the linked X account announces a different CA. A recognizable trader appears in a holdings snapshot. The thesis is worth considering, the contract mismatch is unresolved, and the snapshot does not tell you whether that trader is buying or exiting. These are three findings, not a buy signal.

How to investigate it

Keep one brief record per check with source and check time: thesis/meta/upside; bundles, X and exact-CA consistency plus obvious sell or liquidity issues; notable participants and observed behavior. Separate observed facts from the upside judgment. Mark unverified information Unknown. Use 202A.11 to decide the depth and trading approach.

Check your reasoning — answered

A token has a working X link and a known trader holds it. Has it passed all three checks? No. Neither fact explains fresh demand or clears bundles and contract mismatches. A holding snapshot also does not establish accumulation. Complete the minimal checks before shaping a trade.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Snipe

Use listing context, sampled flow in Inspect, and followed-wallet snapshots as leads. Verify bundles, contract links, sellability, and wallet behavior externally. No badge is not proof of absence.

Go deeper

CA means contract address; KOL means key opinion leader. A working X link is only a consistency check, not proof that the token is legitimate. Compare exact contracts rather than names, verify any claimed replacement against primary announcements, and mark unverified information Unknown. A profitable or recognizable wallet is not automatically supportive: entry timing, position size, remaining inventory, and selling matter. A balance snapshot alone cannot establish buying or selling. Upside is a reasoned case about possible demand, not a promised target.
